data.title: BMO Capital Upgrades Bloom Energy (BE) Stock. What's Driving the Optimism?
data.description:
BMO Capital analyst Ameet Thakkar upgraded his rating on Bloom Energy (BE), a provider of solid oxide fuel cell systems, to Buy from Hold after meetings with management reinforced his optimism about the company's commercial momentum and recent execution. Moreover, Thakkar believes that the risk-reward is more attractive following the recent pullback.

The analyst lowered his price target on BE stock to $230 from $260 to reflect multiple compression amid the recent selloff across power infrastructure players.

BMO Capital Turns Bullish on Bloom Energy

Thakkar said he was previously cautious about Bloom Energy, looking for "large-scale proof-of-concept" and the durability of the company's higher-cost generation solution once turbine and grid capacity become more available. The analyst was also cautious due to the company's dependence on U.S. data center demand.

While these concerns persist, he contends that the setup has improved and the stock's risk-reward looks more attractive following the recent pullback. Thakkar added that his 2027 estimates remain above the Street's expectations, and large projects, including the deal with Nebius (NBIS), provide proof of solid execution he was previously seeking.

Furthermore, Thakkar highlighted improved optimism about contractual protections, milestone-based customer payments, and project financing. He also noted Bloom Energy's ability to expand manufacturing and potential to bring down costs. Thakkar also emphasized that the company is increasingly being considered for initial power-system design, rather than just as an alternative when conventional power is unavailable.

The analyst expects Bloom Energy to generate about $7.88 billion in revenue in 2027, "though initial guidance could also pose key near-term risk." Thakkar said that over the longer term, valuation depends on BE's total addressable market (TAM) expanding beyond U.S. data centers to international deployments and broader commercial and industrial demand. He also sees prospects in utility generation. Overall, Thakkar believes that the key debate is less about manufacturing capacity and more about whether Bloom Energy can sustain multi-gigawatt demand and strong economics as current power shortages ease.

Is BE Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Despite declining 26% over the past month, BE stock is still up 93% year-to-date amid demand for the company's fuel-cell technology in AI data centers. Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Bloom Energy stock based on 13 Buys and eight holds.

The average BE stock price target of $293.50 indicates about 74.6% upside potential.

data.title: Nvidia Stock Could Plunge to $100, Warns Investor. Here's Why
data.description:
What started as a promising Thursday for Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) investors has turned into another disappointing session. After surging nearly 5% earlier in the day, the chip giant has reversed course, falling 3.3% as uncertainty continues to weigh on the broader market. The latest reversal leaves Nvidia shares 38% below their October peak and down 21% since the beginning of 2026. Concerns surrounding its leadership transition, extensive spending commitments, and the sustainability of AI infrastructure investments continue weighing on sentiment.

And if investor Sungarden Investment is correct, the worst may still lie ahead. Despite Nvidia's already steep losses, the investor believes the stock could tumble all the way to $100 over the next 12 to 18 months. His warning rests primarily on technical indicators and broader market conditions, suggesting that Nvidia's troubles extend well beyond the controversy surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang.

Sungarden's bearish outlook begins with a comparison between current trading patterns and previous market downturns. Although Nvidia has recovered from several steep sell-offs over the past decade, the investor believes this episode could prove far more damaging.

"While I always account for the possibility that any stock or ETF can manage yet another big leg up, I think the odds are against NVDA this time," Sungarden noted.

Sungarden believes institutional selling could continue overwhelming buying interest, preventing a lasting recovery despite Nvidia's technological advantages. The investor also points to deteriorating liquidity, suggesting that large investment funds may be reducing their exposure to leading tech companies.

Another concern involves the financial relationships supporting the industry's rapid expansion, where investments move between cloud providers, developers, and semiconductor manufacturers. Sungarden points out that these arrangements could become problematic for Nvidia if financing slows, while Huang's departure introduces additional uncertainty surrounding strategic direction.

However, the investor considers broader trading mechanics more important than any individual controversy, especially when examining heavily weighted equities like Nvidia during prolonged market downturns.

"In a liquidity-driven unwind, the generals are always the last to get taken out. And their drop is the steepest," Sungarden explained.

Essentially, Sungarden argues that Nvidia's dominant position within passive portfolios could become a liability when investors withdraw capital from index funds. Those withdrawals could increase selling pressure on heavily weighted stocks like Nvidia, potentially creating additional downward momentum regardless of underlying financial performance.

His Nvidia chart analysis also reveals deteriorating momentum, with several important moving averages already broken and successive rallies failing to establish stronger price levels.

Ultimately, Sungarden offers a particularly bearish forecast for investors expecting Nvidia to recover its previous valuation: "To $100, more likely than back to $240, its previous peak level, over the next 12-18 months." (To watch Sungarden Investment's track record, click here)

With Nvidia trading near $147 on Thursday, that scenario implies another 32% downside, potentially extending an already costly retreat for long-term holders.

While Sungarden sees further losses ahead for Nvidia, most Wall Street analysts remain bullish on the company's long-term prospects. Nvidia currently has a Moderate Buy consensus rating, based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and just one Sell assigned over the past three months. The average 12-month price target stands at $232.59, representing 59% upside from current levels. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: Market Looks for Direction After Big Selloff
data.description:
U.S. equity markets are looking for direction after a big selloff on Nov. 19 and the market debut of artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic (ANT). The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,100 points or 2.19% on the day. The benchmark S&P 500 index fell 2.02%, and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite dropped 550 points or 2.25%.

The latest selloff continues a downward trend for stocks as investors move money out of equities. Over the past month, the S&P 500 stock index has fallen 10% and entered a correction, according to data from Reuters (TRI). The downward pressure on stocks has led the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), Wall Street's fear gauge, to reach 29, its highest level since March of this year, according to CNBC.

In the futures market, the Dow is up 0.02%, the S&P 500 is down 0.04%, and the Nasdaq is declining 0.23%.

Anthropic's Market Debut

Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT." The stock was priced at $83 a share and opened trading at $111.50. However, ANT stock quickly fell more than 10% from that peak to finish trading at $97.17 per share, up 17% in its market debut.

Regarding what's likely to move markets in the next trading session, economic data on Nov. 20 is relatively light. However, the University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment reading for November will be released before the market opens in New York. The reading should provide an important look at how American consumers are feeling heading into the year-end holiday shopping season.

Wall Street is likely to continue watching the performance of ANT stock and its implications for the AI trade.

Is ANT Stock a Buy?

Anthropic's stock has a consensus Strong Buy rating among six Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on five Buy and one Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average ANT price target of $134 implies 38% upside from current levels.

data.title: Palo Alto Networks Stock Jumps as AI Cyber Threats Create New Growth Opportunity
data.description:
Shares of cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks (PANW) jumped on Thursday after the company lifted its annual outlook. Meanwhile, CEO Nikesh Arora warned that serious software vulnerabilities are being discovered at nearly seven times last year's monthly average. This could benefit Palo Alto by increasing demand for its virtual patching and AI security services, which would help the company generate additional recurring revenue.

Arora explained on Wednesday that security teams are struggling to install software fixes fast enough. Meanwhile, a recent AI-assisted hacking campaign targeted at least 19 organizations, with attackers gaining unauthorized access to systems or data at 10 of them.

Researchers from Palo Alto's Unit 42 division uncovered the operation, which took place during August and September. The attackers used an open-source AI tool called Cairn to carry out 25 operations. At one organization, more than one million personal records were exposed. The software could plan attacks and adjust its approach without requiring someone to oversee every step.

This creates another problem for businesses. Even when software developers release security updates, companies cannot always install them immediately without the risk of disruptions to their systems. Arora expects that the heavy workload associated with these updates could continue for at least another 18 months.

Catalysts That May Push the Stock Higher

The growing number of software vulnerabilities could increase demand for Palo Alto's virtual patching service, which protects vulnerable systems while companies prepare permanent fixes. Palo Alto already serves nearly 70,000 network security customers, giving it a sizable existing customer base for the service.

Meanwhile, demand for AI security is already contributing to the company's growth. Its Prisma AIRS product reached nearly $170 million in annual recurring revenue within five quarters of becoming available, with more than 1,000 customers using the platform. Furthermore, traffic generated by AI agents on Palo Alto's network security platform increased about ninefold year-over-year.

Yesterday's earnings provided additional evidence of strong cybersecurity spending. Fiscal first-quarter revenue grew by 39% to $3.44 billion, while next-generation security annual recurring revenue increased by 66% to $9.73 billion.

Risks to Watch Out For

However, the sevenfold increase refers to discovered software vulnerabilities, not successful cyberattacks. AI can also help security teams find weaknesses before hackers exploit them. Therefore, the longer-term effect on cybersecurity spending remains uncertain.

Additionally, Palo Alto faces competition from other security providers, and some customers may prefer upgrading their existing tools rather than purchasing additional services.

The company's valuation is another consideration. Palo Alto trades at roughly 82 times the midpoint of its projected Fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of $4.26 to $4.30 per share. This leaves less room for disappointing results if demand for its newer AI security products slows down.

Is PANW Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on PANW stock. This is based on 32 Buys and eight Holds assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average PANW price target of $423.43 per share implies 17.1% upside potential. (See PANW Stock Forecast).

data.title: 3 'Strong Buy' Data Center Stocks to Watch After Anthropic's Record IPO
data.description:
AI developer Anthropic (ANT) began trading on Thursday on Nasdaq. It raised a record $81.34 billion in its initial public offering (IPO), above its earlier target due to strong demand. This has drawn fresh attention to the AI trade. For investors looking for other ways to gain exposure to the industry, analysts remain bullish on three less popular data center-related names: Willdan Group (WLDN), Comfort Systems (FIX), and Graham Corporation (GHM). Each stock carries a Strong Buy rating from analysts with at least 50% upside, according to TipRanks' Compare Top Data Center Stocks tool.

GHM has rallied the most year-to-date, up 23% to about $77 per share. However, Willdan offers the biggest upside of 78%.

These companies are among the "pick and shovels" of the AI buildout. They provide the physical infrastructure that powers the data center boom.

Willdan Group (WLDN)

Willdan is an American engineering and construction company. It helps companies maximize their energy systems and modernize their electric grids. It also offers consulting on building and safety guidance.

The company's clients span utilities, government agencies, and private businesses.

Willdan's shares are currently down about 29% year-to-date. However, analysts continue to rate the stock a Strong Buy and see about 78% upside in the months ahead. This is based on an average price target of $130.

Comfort Systems (FIX)

Comfort provides mechanical, electrical, and plumbing contracting services. The Texas-based firm helps clients install, maintain, and retrofit their heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems.

Comfort Systems' shares are up about 22% since the start of the year. Interestingly, analysts see room for an even bigger rally. They expect the stock to rally by 67% in the months ahead. This is based on the average price target of $1,849.

Graham Corporation (GHM)

Graham is an American industrial engineering and manufacturing company. The New York-based business makes fluid, power, heat transfer, and vacuum technologies.

Graham produces several items, including condensers, cryogenic pumps, and ejectors. Other products include turbines, generators, cooling systems, and thermal-control electronics. Its products are used in data centers to cool AI systems.

Graham's shares are up 23% year-to-date to about $77 per share. Analysts see room for another 56% rally over the coming months. This is based on an average price target of $120.50.

data.title: U.S. Market Sells Off as Anthropic Goes Public
data.description:
Anthropic's (ANT) highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO) was not enough to lift the U.S. stock market higher on Nov. 19. Despite extensive media coverage and hype surrounding the Anthropic IPO, markets sold off sharply on the day, with the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average plunging 1,100 points or 2.19%. The benchmark S&P 500 index lost 2.02% and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite plunged 550 points or 2.25%.

The latest selloff continues a trend of declines on Wall Street as investors turn risk averse and move money out of equities. In the past five trading sessions, the S&P 500 has declined 6%. Over the past month, the leading U.S. stock index has fallen 10%. Market data from CNBC shows that the most pain continues to be felt in technology stocks and companies closely tied to artificial intelligence (AI).

Chipmakers Nvidia (NVDA) and Micron Technology (MU) gave up their initial gains on the day and fell, along with technology giants Microsoft (MSFT) and Meta Platforms (META). The stock of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) lost 8% after short seller Hunterbrook Capital released a report alleging that the company has violated U.S. export controls and sold its products in China.

Anthropic's Performance

Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq index under the ticker symbol "ANT." The stock was priced at $83 a share and opened trading at $111.50, a 34% jump. However, ANT stock quickly fell more than 10% from that peak to finish trading at $97.17 per share, up 17% in its market debut.

The major U.S. averages fell to session lows immediately after Anthropic's stock started trading as investors appeared to take profits and continued shifting money out of the AI trade. The steep selloff on Nov. 19 led the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), known as Wall Street's fear gauge, to reach 29, its highest level since March of this year. CNBC said the reading indicates rising levels of anxiety among investors.

Stock Winners and Losers

Stocks that outperformed on Nov. 19 included:

  • Palo Alto Networks (PANW)
  • Okta (OKTA)
  • Western Digital (WDC)
  • Chevron (CVX)
  • CrowdStrike (CRWD)

Equities that underperformed included:

  • CoreWeave (CRWV)
  • Shopify (SHOP)
  • DoorDash (DASH)
  • Salesforce (CRM)
  • Amazon (AMZN)

data.title: Anthropic Stock Is Attracting Over $1 Billion in Retail Trading. Here's What's Happening
data.description:
Retail investors rushed to trade shares of Claude AI developer Anthropic (ANT) on Thursday, with their total first-day trading activity projected to reach a record $1.4 billion. According to Bloomberg, Vanda Research expects individual investors to purchase a net $80 million to $90 million worth of shares, which would make Anthropic's debut the third-biggest IPO trading day for retail inflows. The activity followed Anthropic's $111.50 opening price, which was 34.3% above its $83 IPO price.

The difference between those figures is important. Net buying measures how much investors purchase after accounting for sales, while trading turnover includes both purchases and sales. Therefore, the projected $1.4 billion in turnover suggests that investors are actively trading Anthropic rather than simply buying shares to hold.

Vanda recorded $18.6 million in net retail purchases during Anthropic's first 30 minutes of trading. That was lower than expected, as the research firm had previously projected $250 million in first-day net purchases.

Even so, the updated $80 million to $90 million estimate would trail only space company SpaceX (SPCX), which attracted $118 million in June 2026, and cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase (COIN), which recorded $92 million in 2021.

Anthropic's Debut Draws Money Away From Other AI Stocks

However, some of the money entering Anthropic appears to be coming from existing AI investments. Vanda strategist Viraj Patel reported that retail traders were selling other AI stocks to fund their Anthropic purchases. Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was among the companies experiencing selling pressure, although its shares also fell after short-selling firm Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a bearish position and questioned the company's business ties to China.

Meanwhile, Patel said that buying interest in AI chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA), another popular stock among individual investors, had fallen.

Anthropic's record IPO also attracted demand from investors who wanted more shares than they received. According to The Wall Street Journal, retail investors received about 15% of the $81.34 billion public offering, compared with the maximum 20% allocation previously discussed.

Steven Quirk, chief brokerage officer at trading platform Robinhood Markets (HOOD), told Bloomberg that its customers wanted considerably more Anthropic shares than they received. However, every Robinhood customer who requested shares received at least one.

Is ANT Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on ANT stock. This is based on five Buys assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average ANT price target is $134 per share. (See ANT Stock Forecast).

data.title: Skydance Stock (NYSE:SKYD) Down Over 5% as it Bows Out of World Cup Rights
data.description:
The bidding for World Cup rights apparently got too rich for the blood of entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD), as it pulled out of the bidding, according to a report from Bloomberg. This actually makes a certain amount of sense, especially given Skydance's post-merger priorities, but it will still likely hurt some viewers. Skydance stock dropped over 5% in the closing minutes of Thursday's trading. Skydance has seen a 57.14% loss in its share price over the past year.

We Have Soccer at Home

It might seem like a bad idea for Skydance to bow out of the bidding for the World Cup. The tournaments are supposed to bring in as much as $4 billion, with reports suggesting that $2 billion of that will come from the 2030 round while another $1 billion to $1.5 billion will come in for 2034. But Skydance's co-chief executive officer, David Ellison, made it clear that Skydance was going to be "disciplined" when it came to buying future sports media.

Given that Skydance owes somewhere in the neighborhood of $80 billion in debt outstanding since the merger, it makes sense that it would not want to shell out another $4 billion on top of that for a sporting event. Granted, that sporting event would have brought in quite a bit in ad revenue, but it's still a lot of money given what Skydance currently owes. Worse yet, the 2034 round of World Cup play will take place in Saudi Arabia, the report noted, and that represents a time zone issue that might be tougher for American audiences to get behind.

A New Bit of Science Fiction

Meanwhile, Skydance's David Ellison is taking something of a personal hand in a major, $100 million project that recently signed Chris Pratt to its cast list, noted a report from Page Six Hollywood. The movie is called The Traveler, and focuses on time travel, which apparently is enough to get Ellison himself interested.

The Traveler took on a bit of cachet in 2019, when it showed up on the Black List, an annual list that focused on unproduced Hollywood projects. Based on a novel, it focuses on a time traveler who would rather not be traveling through time, as well as his son, who shares a bond with his father that is never quite broken, even across thousands of years. It is considered an "elevated" science fiction story, the report noted, which may give Skydance a means to get out from under Star Trek as its primary science fiction connection.

Is Skydance a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on SKYD stock based on five Buys, five Holds and five Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average SKYD price target of $9.50 per share implies 50.79% upside potential.

data.title: Stock Market Selloff Hits Every Sector as Consumer Stocks Lead Declines
data.description:
U.S. stocks sold off on Thursday afternoon, with all 11 major S&P 500 sectors declining as investors pulled back from riskier assets. The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) showed the smallest loss at 0.55%, while the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY) fell by 2.29%. The selloff followed an early rally that was fueled by AI developer Anthropic's (ANT) stock market debut. However, enthusiasm faded as investors continued to assess the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.

Minutes from the Fed's October meeting, released on Wednesday, showed that nearly all officials expected further rate increases if the economy performed as projected. Higher borrowing costs can discourage consumers from making expensive purchases, which adds pressure to businesses that depend on discretionary spending.

Meanwhile, the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV) declined by 1.98%, making it the second-worst-performing sector. The Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) followed with a 1.85% loss.

Why Energy Stocks Are Holding Up Better Than Other Sectors

Energy's relative strength came as oil prices recovered from Wednesday's losses. According to Reuters, fresh reports of tanker disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz supported crude prices despite concerns about excess global supply. However, the recovery was limited by Wednesday's U.S. inventory report, which showed that crude stockpiles increased by 3.4 million barrels.

Elsewhere, the Industrial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLI) dropped by 1.61%, while the Materials Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLB) fell by 1.67%. These declines came as concerns about higher interest rates weighed on expectations for economic activity.

Even traditionally defensive sectors struggled. The Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU) declined by 1.07%, while the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP) lost 1.33%.

Meanwhile, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) fell by 1.27% despite the earlier AI-driven rally. The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) slipped by 1.30%, while the Real Estate Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLRE) declined by 1.28%.

The bond market also showed signs of caution. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield stood near 5.05%, while the CBOE Volatility Index had climbed by 13.8% to 27.95.

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), which tracks the overall stock market in the U.S. This is based on 415 Buys, 82 Holds, and six Sells assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average SPY price target of $905.59 per share implies 25.7% upside potential. (See SPY Stock Forecast).
